item.title: Annalise.ai
item.description:
Annalise.ai builds radiology AI that looks for many findings at once rather than one condition per algorithm. Its chest X-ray product covers a long list of abnormalities, and its brain CT product targets urgent findings such as bleeds.

Results are shown to the radiologist with the suspicious area marked, and the tool can help prioritize urgent studies in a worklist.

It is sold to hospitals and imaging groups. Output needs radiologist review, and local validation matters. Alternatives include Aidoc, Lunit, Qure.ai, and Gleamer. Annalise.ai suits radiology departments that want broad coverage from one vendor.

item.title: ATLAS.ti
item.description:
It supports document coding, memos, networks, and co-occurrence tables. AI coding and summary features suggest codes and condense text, and researchers can accept or edit them. It runs on desktop and in a browser.

It is used in academic research, UX research, and market research. Licenses are sold in student, academic, and business tiers.

NVivo and MAXQDA are the main alternatives. ATLAS.ti suits researchers who want flexible coding and visual network tools.

item.title: Autopsy
item.description:
Examiners add a disk image and run ingest modules that find deleted files, web history, and keyword hits. Timelines and hash databases help organize findings. Plug-ins extend it.

It is used by law enforcement, corporate investigators, and students. Reports must be validated before use in court.

Magnet AXIOM and Cellebrite are commercial alternatives. Autopsy suits forensic scientists with limited budgets.

item.title: Brainomix
item.description:
Brainomix is a UK imaging AI company. Its stroke products assess non-contrast CT and angiography scans and give clinicians scores and maps that support treatment decisions.

It also offers lung software that analyzes chest CT for fibrosis, helping track disease over time.

Brainomix is sold to hospitals and health systems. Regulatory status varies by region, so check what is cleared where you work. Alternatives include RapidAI, Viz.ai, and Aidoc. Brainomix suits stroke services and respiratory clinics.

item.title: Diagnocat
item.description:
Diagnocat analyzes dental imaging. A clinician uploads a CBCT scan, panoramic radiograph, or intraoral X-rays, and the AI segments the teeth and bone and flags issues in a report organized by tooth.

For orthodontics, the 3D view helps with impacted teeth, root position, and airway or bone assessment, and the reports can be shared with patients or referring dentists.

Diagnocat is a paid service. Findings are decision support, so the dentist has to confirm them. Alternatives include Overjet, Pearl, and VideaHealth. Diagnocat suits practices that use CBCT regularly.

item.title: FL Studio
item.description:
The pattern-based step sequencer and piano roll make it quick to sketch ideas. It comes with synths, samplers, and effects, and includes stem separation. Image-Line has a lifetime free updates policy.

Editions differ by feature set and price.

Ableton Live and Logic Pro are alternatives. FL Studio suits producers who start from beats.

item.title: Gleamer
item.description:
Gleamer is a French radiology AI company known for tools that find fractures on X-rays and for a chest X-ray product. Findings appear as marked overlays inside the radiologist’s viewer.

Its products are grouped in a suite for emergency and routine imaging, and the company has expanded toward other modalities such as MRI.

Gleamer is sold to hospitals and imaging centers. Overlays are an aid, not a diagnosis. Alternatives include Annalise.ai, Qure.ai, Lunit, and Aidoc. Gleamer suits emergency and musculoskeletal imaging workflows.

item.title: Google Earth Engine
item.description:
It hosts decades of satellite and climate datasets, such as Landsat and Sentinel. Users write scripts in JavaScript or Python to compute change over time, such as forest loss or sea ice. Results export to maps and tables.

It is free for research and education, with commercial plans for business use.

QGIS and ArcGIS work with local data. Earth Engine suits climate scientists and geospatial analysts.

item.title: HeartFlow
item.description:
HeartFlow analyzes coronary CT angiography. Its software builds a 3D model of the heart arteries and estimates how blocked vessels affect blood flow, and a plaque analysis service quantifies buildup.

The goal is to give cardiologists more information from a noninvasive scan so fewer patients need invasive angiography.

It is a paid clinical service, typically ordered through hospitals. Alternatives include Cleerly and Tempus’s cardiac tools. HeartFlow suits cardiology teams that already use cardiac CT.

item.title: Houdini
item.description:
Instead of editing a model by hand, you build a network of nodes that describes how it is made. Change one input and the whole result updates, which makes it easy to produce variations or redo a shot after a director changes their mind. Its simulation tools for fluids, particles, cloth, and rigid bodies are a main reason studios adopt it.

Film VFX teams, game studios, and motion designers use it, and it connects to engines such as Unreal and Unity through plugins. The learning curve is long, since you need to think in networks rather than in tools.

item.title: Imagen AI
item.description:
Photographers upload past edits to build a personal profile. Imagen then edits new shoots and returns adjustments to Lightroom or Photoshop. It also includes culling and cropping tools.

It is billed per photo or by plan.

Aftershoot and Lightroom presets are alternatives. Imagen suits photographers who edit thousands of images.

item.title: KeyShot
item.description:
Users drag materials onto a model, set up lighting, and see the render update live. It reads files from CAD tools such as SolidWorks and Rhino. KeyShot also includes AI-based features for texture and background creation in newer versions.

It is a paid product with subscription and perpetual options.

Blender Cycles and V-Ray are alternatives. KeyShot suits industrial designers and jewelry designers who need product renders fast.

item.title: MegaDetector
item.description:
It runs on large folders of photos and outputs boxes and confidence scores. Researchers then sort detections or pass them to species classifiers. Microsoft AI for Good started the project.

Accuracy varies with camera setup, and some manual review is still expected.

Wildlife Insights offers a web service. MegaDetector suits zoologists and wildlife biologists with large image sets.

item.title: Observable
item.description:
Users write code in notebooks, and charts update as data changes. Observable Plot offers a concise chart API, and Observable Framework builds static data apps. Teams share notebooks and dashboards.

It requires some JavaScript knowledge, which is a barrier for non-coders.

Datawrapper and Flourish are no-code alternatives. Observable suits data visualization specialists who code.

item.title: PixInsight
item.description:
It uses scripts and process modules for tasks like background extraction, noise reduction, and deconvolution. Add-ons use machine learning for noise and star removal. Photographers work in a non-destructive way and save workflows.

The interface is technical, and beginners usually take time to learn it. It is sold as a license.

Siril is a free alternative, and Photoshop is used for finishing. PixInsight suits serious astrophotographers.

item.title: RapidAI
item.description:
RapidAI makes software for time-critical imaging. For suspected stroke, it processes CT or MRI scans, identifies large vessel occlusions and measures tissue at risk, then alerts the team.

Its platform also covers aneurysm and other vascular conditions and helps coordinate transfers between hospitals.

It is sold to hospitals and stroke networks. Results guide care but do not replace clinical judgment. Alternatives include Viz.ai, Aidoc, and Brainomix. RapidAI suits stroke centers and their referring hospitals.

item.title: Rhino
item.description:
Rhino models curves and surfaces with high accuracy. Grasshopper lets designers build parametric definitions with nodes, so changing a number updates a whole design. A large plug-in ecosystem covers rendering, fabrication, and analysis.

It is sold as a perpetual license rather than a subscription. The learning curve is moderate for basic modeling and steeper for Grasshopper.

SketchUp and Revit overlap in some uses. Rhino suits architects and designers who work with complex geometry.

item.title: Subtle Medical
item.description:
Subtle Medical builds AI that sits on top of existing scanners. Its tools denoise and enhance images, which lets sites shorten MRI scans or reduce the dose in PET and contrast-enhanced studies.

Imaging centers use it to raise throughput and make exams easier on patients, without replacing their hardware.

It is sold to hospitals and imaging centers. Results depend on scanner and protocol, so sites validate before changing clinical practice. Alternatives include vendor-built reconstruction tools from scanner makers. Subtle suits imaging departments focused on speed and dose.

item.title: Taranis
item.description:
Images from planes or drones are analyzed to find issues at the leaf level. Reports guide agronomists to problem areas. Insights integrate with farm management tools.

It is a commercial service with custom pricing.

DroneDeploy and Climate FieldView offer related imagery. Taranis suits crop consultants and agronomists.

item.title: TinEye
item.description:
It finds copies, edits, and earlier versions, and sorts by date. Fact-checkers use it to trace the origin of a photo. A browser extension and API are available.

Coverage is limited to images it has indexed, so a lack of matches is not proof of originality.

Google Lens and Yandex Images are alternatives. TinEye suits fact-checkers verifying images.

item.title: Unreal Engine
item.description:
The engine includes a visual scripting system called Blueprints, so people can build gameplay without writing C++. Lumen handles dynamic lighting and Nanite handles very detailed geometry, which suits cinematic scenes. MetaHuman Creator, which runs with the engine, produces realistic digital characters.

Game studios, film and TV productions, car makers, and architecture firms all use it. The editor is free to download, and Epic takes a royalty on products above a revenue threshold, with separate terms for some non-game uses. Check Epic’s licensing page for current terms.

item.title: UrbanFootprint
item.description:
Planners test how zoning changes or new development affect housing, jobs, and transportation. Built-in datasets cover parcels, demographics, and mobility. Results can be shared as maps and reports.

It targets professional planning teams and uses custom pricing.

ArcGIS and Carto offer related capabilities. UrbanFootprint suits city planners.

item.title: VideaHealth
item.description:
VideaHealth is an AI system for dental radiographs. It reviews X-rays as they are taken and highlights suspected decay, bone loss, and other issues on the image.

It is aimed at practices and dental service organizations that want a second read and a shared standard of diagnosis, and the marked images help when explaining treatment to patients.

VideaHealth is sold on subscription. Dentists must confirm every finding. Alternatives include Overjet, Pearl, and Diagnocat. VideaHealth suits practices that want radiograph review built into daily workflow.

item.title: Windy
item.description:
Pilots, sailors, paragliders, and outdoor guides use it to see how conditions change by altitude and hour. Layers include radar, satellite, cloud tops, and wave height. The premium plan adds extra data and removes ads.

Forecasts are model output, not guarantees, so users should compare models and check local reports when conditions are marginal.

AccuWeather and Tomorrow.io are alternatives with different focus. Windy suits anyone who needs detailed wind and weather layers.

item.title: Wolfram Mathematica
item.description:
Users work in notebooks that combine code, results, and text. The Wolfram Language has built-in functions for a huge range of math and data tasks. It connects with Wolfram Alpha knowledge and, in newer versions, with language model tools.

Licenses are paid, and student editions are cheaper.

MATLAB and SageMath are alternatives. Mathematica suits mathematicians who need symbolic power.

item.title: Adobe Photoshop
item.description:
Photoshop is the image editor most photographers, retouchers, and designers learn first. It works on pixels in layers, with masks, selections, adjustment layers, and blend modes that let you change one part of an image without touching the rest. Photo retouching, product shots, poster layouts, and web graphics all fit into that same layer-based workflow, which is why files and techniques carry from one studio to the next.

The AI features sit inside that workflow instead of replacing it. Generative Fill takes a selection and a short text prompt and creates new content that matches the lighting and perspective around it. Generative Expand extends the canvas past the original edges, and the Remove tool erases distractions like power lines or stray people. Select Subject and Neural Filters handle selections, portrait adjustments, and colorization with less manual work. Generated content arrives on its own layer, so you can mask it, blend it, or throw it away.

item.title: Azure AI Vision
item.description:
Azure AI Vision gives developers pretrained image analysis. The Image Analysis service can describe an image in a sentence, tag objects and scenes, detect people and objects with locations, and extract printed and handwritten text through OCR. Additional capabilities include background removal, smart cropping, and searching images by meaning, using models that understand both text and images.

Video and spatial analysis features can analyze camera feeds to count people and measure how they move through physical spaces, useful in retail and building management. Face-related features exist but are limited by a responsible AI approval process, since facial recognition has privacy and fairness concerns. Customers can also train custom models for their own image categories, and containers allow running some features on the edge.

item.title: Bria
item.description:
Bria builds visual generative AI around licensing. Its models are trained on licensed data from content partners rather than scraped web images, and contributors share in revenue, which gives companies a clearer position on copyright than many alternatives. The company also offers indemnification to enterprise customers.

The product is delivered as APIs and tools for businesses. Capabilities include generating images from prompts, editing and background removal, creating product shots, and controls for brand consistency. Enterprises in advertising, e-commerce, and media can embed these features in their apps, with options for fine-tuning on their own assets.

item.title: Builder.io
item.description:
Builder.io bridges developers and non-developers. Engineers integrate it into a website built with React, Vue, Next.js, or other frameworks, registering their components, and marketers and designers then assemble and edit pages visually using those components without waiting for a code release. That reduces bottlenecks for landing pages, campaigns, and content, while code stays under developers’ control.

AI has become central. Visual Copilot converts Figma designs into code in a chosen framework and styling approach, using the team’s own components where possible, which cuts down on the tedious work of translating designs. Newer offerings let teams describe features and have an AI agent build and update applications. A headless CMS manages structured content, and personalization and A/B testing features help optimize pages.

item.title: Cartoon Animator
item.description:
Cartoon Animator is built to make 2D animation approachable. You can bring in artwork, a photo, or one of the included characters, add a bone rig, and animate the character. Face tracking from a webcam drives expressions, motion templates provide walks and gestures, and audio can generate lip movement automatically.

The software includes tools for composing scenes, with backgrounds, props, and cameras, and it can export videos, image sequences, and assets for editors. It also links to Reallusion’s other products. Users can bring in layered files from Photoshop and Clip Studio, which helps artists who draw their own characters.

item.title: Cavalry
item.description:
Cavalry offers a different way to make motion graphics. Instead of placing keyframes for each property, you build systems: duplicate a shape in a grid, add a noise behavior, connect values with expressions, and see the animation emerge. Changing one parameter updates the whole piece, which makes iteration quick for design-heavy work such as logo animations, generative patterns, and loops.

It combines 2D vector design, animation, and rendering. Features include a timeline, a node-based graph for connections, text and font tools, and the ability to import vector and bitmap assets. It exports video, sequences, and Lottie, and has tools for creating assets for social media and games. Scripting allows custom behaviors for technical artists.

item.title: DaVinci Resolve
item.description: DaVinci Resolve started as a color grading system used on Hollywood films and grew into a complete post-production suite. It combines a video editor, the Color page for grading, Fusion for visual effects and motion graphics, Fairlight for audio mixing, and a delivery page for exporting. Because all of these are in one application, a project can move from edit to color to sound without being exported or relinked. It runs on Windows, macOS, and Linux.

item.title: Digital Diagnostics
item.description:
Digital Diagnostics offers autonomous AI for eye screening. A clinic staff member takes photos of a patient’s retina with a compatible camera, the software analyzes the images, and within minutes the clinic gets a result: either the screening is negative, or the patient should see an eye specialist. No ophthalmologist needs to read the images.

That matters because many people with diabetes skip yearly eye exams, and early detection of retinopathy prevents vision loss. Putting screening in a primary care office makes it easier to catch disease. The company also develops AI for other conditions and works with health systems on implementation and billing.

item.title: Foxglove
item.description:
Foxglove helps robotics teams understand what their machines did. Robots generate streams from cameras, lidar, GPS, motors, and logs, and debugging requires looking at them together on a timeline. Foxglove’s viewer shows images, point clouds, plots, maps, and 3D scenes in customizable panels that stay synchronized, and it works with ROS and other frameworks.

The platform adds data management. Teams upload recordings to the cloud, search across them by metadata and events, share links to specific moments, and collaborate on issues. The company also created MCAP, an open container format for multimodal robotics data that is now used widely, including as the default recording format in ROS 2.

item.title: GIMP
item.description: GIMP, the GNU Image Manipulation Program, has been a mainstay of free software for decades. It handles photo retouching, compositing, and digital painting with layers, masks, curves, selection tools, brushes, and a large set of filters. It reads and writes many file formats, including PSD files to a degree, and supports scripting in Python and Script-Fu for automation. The latest major version brought improvements such as non-destructive editing and better color management.

item.title: Google Cloud Vision
item.description:
Google Cloud Vision is a set of pretrained image analysis features available through an API. Send an image, and it can return labels describing what it contains, detect objects and their locations, read printed and handwritten text, identify landmarks and logos, detect faces and emotions without identifying individuals, and flag explicit content with SafeSearch. It processes single images and batches, including scanned documents.

Typical uses include indexing photo libraries, extracting text from receipts and signs, moderating uploaded images, and powering search by image. Google offers related products for more specialized needs, such as Document AI for forms and Vertex AI for custom models and newer multimodal Gemini models that can describe and reason about images in more detail. Product search features help retailers match photos to catalogs.

item.title: ImageTrend
item.description:
ImageTrend makes software for first responders. Paramedics and EMTs record patient information, treatments, and outcomes on a tablet or computer, producing the report used for handoff to hospitals, billing, and quality review. The data also feeds state and national registries.

The company also provides tools for state EMS offices, trauma and stroke registries, and hospital data collection, as well as analytics for system performance. Newer tools use AI to help reduce documentation time and check data quality.

item.title: Invoke
item.description:
Invoke is built for people who want control over AI images. Beyond typing a prompt, the layered canvas lets users paint, mask, and inpaint specific areas, combine generated elements, and iterate on a composition like in an image editor. Control features guide pose, depth, and structure.

It works with Stable Diffusion and other open models, and users can add their own checkpoints and fine-tunes. The open-source release runs on a local machine with a capable GPU, which keeps images private, and the company provides a hosted version for teams with management features.

item.title: lemlist
item.description:
lemlist helps sales teams and agencies reach prospects at scale. Users build sequences that combine email, LinkedIn steps, and phone tasks, and personalize messages with variables such as name and company. The brand made its name with personalized images and videos that change for each recipient, a way to stand out in crowded inboxes.

Deliverability is a major part of the product. Inbox warm-up gradually builds sender reputation, and tools check domains and monitor placement so emails land in primary inboxes, not spam. A lead database lets users find contacts and verify emails, and AI helps write openers and suggest follow-ups.

item.title: Maltego
item.description:
Maltego is known for visual link analysis. An investigator starts with an entity such as a domain name, email address, or company, then runs transforms that pull related data from sources like DNS records, social media, breach databases, and corporate registries. The results appear as a graph that shows how things connect, which makes patterns easier to see than in a list.

The tool is widely used in cybersecurity and open-source intelligence work. Threat analysts trace infrastructure behind attacks, fraud teams look for networks of related accounts, and journalists and researchers map ownership and connections. A marketplace of data integrations extends what the graph can query, and collaboration features let teams share findings.

item.title: Percy
item.description:
Percy automates visual testing. Developers add it to their test suite, and on each code change it captures screenshots of pages and components across browsers and screen sizes. It compares them with an approved baseline and highlights the pixels that differ, so a reviewer can accept intended changes or catch accidental ones before they reach users.

Visual bugs, such as overlapping text, broken layouts, or missing images, often slip past functional tests, which only check behavior. Percy fills this gap and integrates with pull requests, so design and engineering can review changes together. AI helps ignore noise like anti-aliasing differences or dynamic content, which keeps the review list short.

item.title: Synthflow
item.description:
Synthflow is a no-code voice agent platform. A user designs the call flow in a visual editor, picks a voice, connects a phone number, and the agent handles calls, such as answering questions, booking appointments, and qualifying leads. Integrations connect calendars and CRMs.

Agencies resell the platform with white-label options, building agents for dental offices, home services, and similar businesses. Analytics show call outcomes and transcripts.

Synthflow is paid, with plans by minutes. Voice agents need testing for accuracy and disclosure of AI use. Alternatives include Retell AI, Vapi, Bland AI, Air AI, and PolyAI. Synthflow suits agencies and small businesses deploying voice agents.

item.title: Vuforia
item.description:
Vuforia is one of the longest-running AR toolkits. Developers use its engine to make an app recognize a printed image, a 3D object, or a physical space, and then anchor digital content to it. A technician could point a tablet at a machine and see step-by-step instructions overlaid on the right parts.

PTC has focused it on industry. Vuforia products include tools for creating work instructions, remote expert assistance with live video and annotations, and authoring tools that turn CAD models into AR experiences without much coding. It supports phones, tablets, and headsets, and connects to PTC’s engineering software.

item.title: Winston AI
item.description:
Winston AI is a detection tool for written content. A user pastes text or uploads a document, and the service returns a score estimating how likely it is that AI wrote it, with sentence-level highlighting. A plagiarism checker compares text against web sources, and reports can be shared as evidence.

Publishers use it to screen submissions, teachers to review student work, and agencies to check freelancers. Additional features include detection of AI-generated images and tools aimed at checking whether text has been paraphrased to evade detection. Browser extensions and an API support workflows.

item.title: WordPress
item.description:
WordPress is the software behind a large share of the web. You install it on a web host or sign up with a hosted service, and manage pages, posts, media, and users from a dashboard. A block editor lets you build layouts visually, and thousands of themes control how a site looks. Plugins extend it for SEO, contact forms, memberships, caching, analytics, and online stores through WooCommerce.

It comes in two forms that are easy to confuse. WordPress.org is the free software you host yourself, which gives full control and requires handling hosting, updates, and security. WordPress.com is a hosted service from Automattic with plans that handle those chores. AI arrives mostly through add-ons: Jetpack and other plugins offer writing help, image generation, and chat assistants, and AI site builders can generate a first draft of a site from a prompt. The core project is also adding building blocks for AI features.

item.title: Collov AI
item.description:
Collov AI helps people imagine a space. A user uploads a photo of a room, picks a style such as modern, farmhouse, or minimalist, and the tool produces a redesigned image with furniture and decor. It can also virtually stage an empty room for real estate listings.

Interior designers use it to show clients options early, and real estate agents use it to make listings more appealing. Homeowners use it for ideas before buying furniture. The renders are visualizations and do not reflect exact measurements or the availability of products.

item.title: Datarock
item.description:
Datarock works in mineral exploration. Geologists take photos of drill core samples and log what they see, which is slow and subjective. Datarock’s models analyze the images to identify rock types, measure fractures, and capture structural features, producing consistent digital logs.

The faster, more objective data helps exploration teams make decisions about where to drill next and supports resource modeling. Results integrate with geological software, and the company has expanded to other imagery such as hyperspectral scans and borehole images.

item.title: Eyenuk
item.description:
Eyenuk focuses on automated eye screening. A technician captures retinal images with a compatible camera, and EyeArt analyzes them and reports whether signs of more-than-mild disease are present, flagging patients who need referral. The process takes about a minute and does not need a specialist to read the images.

The purpose is to expand screening for people with diabetes who miss annual eye exams. Primary care clinics, endocrinology practices, and optometrists use it to catch disease earlier. The company has expanded the technology to other conditions and offers versions for different clinical settings.

item.title: Heuritech
item.description:
Heuritech applies computer vision to fashion trends. Its models scan images from social platforms and recognize garments, colors, prints, and shapes, then measure how frequently each appears and how quickly that is changing. The output is a forecast of which items will grow or fade in a market.

Brands use the forecasts to decide what to design, produce, and stock, which can reduce unsold inventory. Reports are segmented by region, age group, and category, and the platform includes tools for tracking competitors and monitoring product performance against trends.

item.title: Seequent
item.description:
Seequent software helps geologists understand what lies underground. Its flagship Leapfrog creates 3D models from drill holes, geophysics, and maps, so teams can see ore bodies and structures, plan drilling, and estimate resources. Other products handle geotechnical data, groundwater, and geophysical modeling.

Mining companies, geotechnical engineers, and environmental consultants use these models for decisions. Cloud tools allow collaboration and centralized data management, and newer features apply machine learning to modeling tasks.

item.title: MagicShot
item.description:
MagicShot takes an all-in-one approach to generative media. Rather than paying for a different service for each task, users get a single workspace for generating images, creating video, building avatars, making product shots, and producing voiceovers, all drawing on one pool of credits.

That suits marketers and small businesses who need a bit of everything. Tools include background replacement, upscaling, style transfer, and templates for ads and social posts. Convenience comes with some compromise, as individual tools may be less advanced than specialized products.

item.title: Free AI Face Swap
item.description:
Free AI Face Swap lets a user upload two photos and exchange the faces. The tool detects faces, aligns them, and blends the result. It runs in the browser, supports common image formats, and offers extra effects around face editing.

People use face swaps for entertainment, memes, and creative projects. The same technology can be misused to create misleading or non-consensual images, so use only photos of people who have agreed, and never use swaps to deceive or harass. Many places have laws about deepfakes and intimate image abuse.

item.title: MagiCrew
item.description:
MagiCrew packages agent capabilities in one open-source system. A general agent can plan and complete tasks with tools, a visual workflow editor lets users build repeatable processes, and messaging and collaboration features let teams work with agents in shared spaces.

Because it is open source, organizations can host it themselves and adapt it, which appeals to teams with privacy requirements or specific needs. It extends an existing open-source project, which gives it a base of users and code to build on.

item.title: Magic Hour
item.description:
Magic Hour brings several AI video tools together. A user can animate a still image, generate a clip from a prompt, convert a video into an anime or painted style, sync a character’s lips to audio, or swap faces. The tools run in the browser and export short videos for social media.

It is aimed at creators and marketers who want a variety of effects without learning several apps. A credit system covers the different features, and templates help with common formats such as memes and talking-head videos.

item.title: BrowserStack Test Companion
item.description:
Test Companion is an AI agent for quality assurance. Instead of a separate dashboard, it works in the developer’s editor, where it can generate test scripts from a description or from the code, run them on BrowserStack’s device and browser cloud, and investigate failures.

Maintenance is a major use. Tests break when interfaces change, and fixing them takes time. The agent can update selectors, adjust steps, and rerun, which reduces the upkeep that makes automated testing costly. It works with common frameworks and connects to BrowserStack’s testing infrastructure.

item.title: Genspark
item.description:
Genspark started as an AI search engine and expanded into an agent workspace. A user states a goal, such as researching a market and building a presentation, and the Super Agent plans the steps, searches the web, uses tools, and produces outputs like slide decks, documents, spreadsheets, and media.

It combines several models and tools behind the scenes, and offers specialized agents for tasks like calling businesses on a user’s behalf, creating images and video, and building simple websites. Results appear in a workspace where users can review and edit them.

item.title: Dataiku
item.description:
Dataiku aims to let analysts, data scientists, and engineers work in the same environment. Teams connect to data sources, clean and prepare data with visual recipes or code, build models, and deploy them as applications or services. The visual interface lowers the barrier for business users, while coders can use notebooks and libraries.

The platform has added tools for generative AI, including connecting to language models, building retrieval applications, and creating agents. Governance features track models and projects, assess risk, and document decisions, which large organizations need to meet internal and regulatory requirements.

item.title: Figma Make
item.description:
Figma Make lets designers and product teams bring ideas to working form. A user describes an app, or starts from a Figma design, and the AI builds an interactive version using code. They can then edit it by chatting, adjusting on the canvas, or changing the code directly.

Because it connects to Figma, designs, components, and styles can serve as the starting point, which keeps results consistent with a design system. Teams use it to test ideas with realistic prototypes before involving engineering, and to share working demos with stakeholders. Backend features such as data storage let prototypes behave more like real apps.

item.title: Gemini Pro
item.description: Gemini Pro refers to the mid-sized models in Google’s Gemini family, positioned between the smaller, cheaper Flash models and the heaviest reasoning options. Google’s naming moves with each generation, but the idea stays the same: Pro is the version intended for demanding everyday work without the cost or delay of the very largest model. Gemini was designed from the start to take in several types of input at once, so the same model reads text, looks at images, listens to audio, and watches video rather than handing those jobs to separate systems.

item.title: GPT Image
item.description:
GPT Image brings image generation into the same model family that handles text. A user describes an image or uploads one to edit, and the model generates or modifies it, following detailed instructions and rendering readable text, which earlier image models struggled with. It can edit photos, change styles, and keep a subject consistent across images.

The model is available inside ChatGPT, where conversation lets users refine results step by step, and through the API for developers building apps. It replaced the DALL-E models in OpenAI’s lineup. Smaller and faster variants exist for cost-sensitive use.

item.title: Qwen Studio
item.description:
Qwen Studio is the consumer-facing way to use Alibaba’s Qwen models. Users chat with the assistant, search the web, upload documents and images for analysis, write code, and generate pictures and video. A mode shows the model’s reasoning for harder problems.

The Qwen family is notable for open-weight releases that developers can download and run, so Qwen Studio doubles as a showcase of what those models can do. It supports many languages, with strong coverage of Chinese and English.

item.title: Stable Diffusion
item.description:
Stable Diffusion changed image generation by being openly available. Rather than a service you rent, the models can be downloaded and run on a consumer GPU, which let anyone generate images privately and without per-image fees. Starting from prompts, the models create pictures in many styles, and later versions improved quality, resolution, and text rendering. Stability AI released several generations, including larger models for higher quality.

A huge ecosystem grew around it. Interfaces such as ComfyUI and Automatic1111 give control over the process, ControlNet guides composition from poses or sketches, and LoRAs let people fine-tune styles or characters with a small number of images. Communities share thousands of models, and hosted services like NightCafe, Leonardo, and Mage.space offer it in the browser. Developers embed the models in applications and pipelines.

item.title: Dang.ai
item.description:
Dang.ai is a place to discover AI tools through community voting. Makers submit their products, users upvote them, and the top entries appear on the homepage. Categories cover writing, image, coding, video, and other areas, with each listing showing a short description and a link.

The model rewards recent launches, so it suits people who want to see what is new and popular. Voting can reflect marketing effort as much as quality, so rankings are a starting point. Comparing listings across several directories gives a better picture.

item.title: Toolify.ai
item.description:
Toolify.ai is a large AI tool directory. Visitors browse categories, search by task, and sort by popularity measures such as estimated monthly traffic and rankings. Each listing has a description, pricing, and links.

Traffic-based ranking offers a different view from editorial picks, showing what people are using. It can favor tools with strong marketing, and estimates are approximate.

The site is free to browse, with paid promotion for makers. Verify claims on the product’s own site. Similar resources include There’s An AI For That, Futurepedia, Aixploria, OpenTools, and Best of AI. Toolify.ai suits people tracking which AI tools are popular.

item.title: Muse Image
item.description:
Muse Image brings Meta’s own image model to its apps. Users describe an image in the Meta AI app, or create pictures in Instagram Stories and WhatsApp, and the model generates it. Meta says the model reasons about a prompt before drawing, rather than mapping text directly to pixels, which helps with complex requests.

Meta plans to extend it to more surfaces, including Facebook, Messenger, and tools for advertisers. Because it is built into apps with billions of users, it makes image creation available to people who would never open a dedicated generator.

item.title: Nano Banana Pro
item.description:
Nano Banana is the name Google gave to its Gemini-based image model, and the Pro version targets higher quality. Users describe an image or edit a photo by instruction, such as changing the background or combining subjects, and the model produces a result that keeps people and objects consistent.

It is known for rendering legible text inside images, producing high-resolution output, and following detailed prompts, which makes it useful for posters, infographics, and product mockups. It is available in the Gemini app, through Google AI Studio and the API, and in other Google products.

item.title: Altern Newsletter
item.description:
The Altern Newsletter comes from Altern, a site that catalogs AI tools. Each issue gathers newly launched products and resources the team found that week, with a short description of what each does. It is organized so a reader can skim for tools relevant to their work.

A weekly cadence keeps it manageable for busy readers. The content leans toward product discovery, not deep analysis, so it works well alongside news-focused newsletters. Items come from the team’s directory and community submissions, which means selection reflects what makers share.

item.title: Igly
item.description:
Igly focuses on product images. A seller uploads photos of items, and the tool removes or replaces backgrounds, places products in lifestyle scenes, adjusts lighting, and creates variations for marketplaces. An infinite canvas lets users arrange and edit many images in one project.

Agents handle multi-step edits from a plain description, such as producing a set of listing images in a consistent style. Presets match the dimensions and rules of common platforms. Sellers use it to reduce the cost of photography and design.

item.title: ZOOOP
item.description:
ZOOOP gathers generative tools on one canvas. A user creates images, video, and audio, arranges them as a project, and collaborates with teammates. AI agents can operate the canvas through an interface, which suits automated workflows.

Instead of a monthly subscription, it uses a consumption model, so people pay for what they generate. That can suit irregular use.

Independent information is limited. Check which models are available and the terms for commercial use. Alternatives include Krea, Freepik, Leonardo AI, Runway, and Flora. ZOOOP suits creators who want flexible pricing and a canvas workflow.

item.title: Cutout.Pro
item.description:
Cutout.Pro offers a set of web tools for common image tasks. Its background remover isolates a subject in a few seconds, and other features upscale resolution, colorize old photos, remove objects, retouch portraits, and generate passport-style photos. A bulk processing option helps stores prepare many product photos.

An API lets developers build these functions into their own products, and plugins connect with tools like Photoshop. Creators and sellers use it for listing photos, social content, and design assets, often at lower cost than hiring a retoucher.

item.title: Gencraft
item.description:
Gencraft aims at casual creators. A user types a description, picks a style such as anime, photo, or fantasy, and gets images in seconds. A mobile app makes it easy to generate avatars, wallpapers, and social media content, and photo transformation tools restyle uploaded pictures.

The platform has added video generation, letting users animate images or generate short clips from prompts. A community feed shows what others create and offers prompts to borrow. The app is designed for experimentation more than for professional workflows.

item.title: Hocoos
item.description:
Hocoos aims at people who want a website without a design process. The user answers questions about their business and style, and the AI generates pages, text, and images, and sets up features such as contact forms, an online store, or appointment booking. An editor allows changes afterward.

The platform includes hosting, a domain option, and SEO basics, plus marketing helpers such as email tools and social media content. It is positioned for small and local businesses and solo entrepreneurs who need an online presence quickly.

item.title: Let's Enhance
item.description:
Let’s Enhance takes a small or low-quality image and makes it larger. The AI adds plausible detail as it increases resolution, so a photo can be printed bigger or used on a high-resolution display with less blur. It also reduces noise and compression artifacts and improves color and lighting.

E-commerce sellers use it to improve product photos, designers to rescue old assets, and photographers to prepare prints. Batch processing and an API handle large volumes, and extra tools cover background removal and image generation.

item.title: Magnific AI
item.description:
Magnific is known as a creative upscaler. Where a standard upscaler sharpens existing pixels, Magnific uses generative AI to invent plausible detail, such as skin texture, fabric, foliage, and architectural elements, guided by a prompt and sliders for how much the image should change. The results can be striking, especially for AI-generated art.

The tool also supports style transfer, relighting, and other transformations, and its capabilities have been added to Freepik’s broader creative platform. Freepik acquired Magnific and kept it as a distinct brand, offering API access to its upscaling features.

item.title: Minimax
item.description:
MiniMax builds models across modalities. Its Hailuo video generator produces short clips from text or images and became popular with creators for motion quality. The company also offers language models, speech synthesis, and music generation, available through apps and an API.

Developers use the API to add generation to products, and the consumer apps let users try the models directly. MiniMax has also released open-weight language models that have been used in agents and coding, adding to its profile among Chinese AI labs.

item.title: Moonvalley
item.description:
Moonvalley builds generative video for creative professionals. Its Marey model is trained on licensed and rights-cleared footage, which the company positions as a safer choice for studios concerned about copyright. Users generate clips and have controls over camera movement, motion, and style.

Filmmakers use it to visualize scenes, build storyboards, and test ideas before expensive shoots, and agencies use it for concept work. The company works with filmmakers and studios, aiming at professional workflows more than casual social content.

item.title: Pachama
item.description:
Pachama works on the trust problem in carbon markets. Credits from forest projects are only valuable if the forest is actually protected or restored, and checking this is hard. Pachama’s models analyze satellite and lidar data to estimate carbon stored in forests and to detect deforestation or degradation over time.

Buyers use its ratings and monitoring to choose credits and track them after purchase, and project developers use the data to support their claims. The company has also worked on tools for measuring forest carbon more cheaply than field surveys alone.

item.title: Palette.fm
item.description:
Palette.fm adds color to old photos. A user uploads a black-and-white image, and the AI predicts plausible colors for skin, clothing, sky, and objects, returning a colorized version in seconds. Different style options change the overall palette, and results can be refined.

Families use it for old portraits, and historians and archivists use it to make collections more engaging. Colorization is an educated guess based on learned patterns, so colors may not match the real scene, and it should not be presented as historically accurate.

item.title: Planable
item.description:
Planable is built around approval workflows. Marketers create posts in a view that looks like the final social post, share it with teammates or clients, collect comments and approvals, and schedule it once signed off. This replaces long email chains and screenshots.

Features include a content calendar, multiple approval stages, and support for many networks. AI tools help draft captions and ideas. Agencies find it useful for client work where sign-off is required.

item.title: Prome AI
item.description:
Prome AI helps designers see concepts early. A user uploads a sketch, a screenshot of a 3D model, or a reference photo and writes a prompt, and the tool produces a realistic rendering with chosen materials, lighting, and style. This speeds up exploration before detailed modeling.

Architects use it for building massing and facades, interior designers for room concepts, and product designers for form studies. Variations can be generated quickly to compare options with clients.

item.title: Stockcake
item.description:
Stockcake offers a searchable library of images made with AI. Users browse or search by topic, preview photos, and download them for use in websites, presentations, and social posts without payment or attribution in many cases. The library is aimed at covering common stock needs.

The advantage is speed and no cost. The drawbacks are those of AI imagery: oddities in hands or text, a generic look, and uncertain legal protection around AI-generated content and likenesses. People depicted are not real, which avoids model release issues.

item.title: Viggle
item.description:
Viggle made character animation easy to try. A user uploads a picture of a character, a person, or a meme figure, picks a motion from a template or uploads a reference video, and the tool produces a video of the character performing it. The physics-based approach gives believable movement.

It went viral for dance and meme videos, and creators use it for short animations, parody, and mockups. Additional features include text prompts for scenes and a mix of motion templates.

item.title: Overjet
item.description:
Overjet is dental AI that reads radiographs. When a dentist takes X-rays, the software outlines suspected cavities, measures bone levels, and identifies calculus and other issues, giving a second look that supports diagnosis and helps explain problems to patients by showing them the marked images.

The technology also serves payers. Insurers use it to review claims and check whether treatment matches findings, and large dental groups use it to standardize care across offices. It has regulatory clearance for several functions in the US.

item.title: Appen
item.description:
Appen is one of the long-standing companies behind AI training data. Machine learning models need large amounts of labeled examples, such as transcribed speech, tagged images, ranked answers, and annotated documents, and Appen supplies them through a global crowd of contributors plus managed teams. Its customers have included major technology companies, and its work has fed search, voice assistants, and recommendation systems.

The services now lean toward generative AI. Appen provides data for aligning large language models, such as human preference rankings, expert-written examples, and red-teaming to find unsafe behavior. It also offers multimodal and speech datasets, coding data, and model evaluation services that test how a system performs in many languages and regions. A platform manages the workflows, quality checks, and contributor payments.

item.title: Applitools
item.description: Applitools solves a problem that ordinary automated tests miss: whether a page looks correct. A functional test can confirm a button exists while the layout is broken, overlapping, or off-screen. Applitools Eyes takes screenshots during tests and compares them to approved baselines using a visual AI that understands layout, text, and color the way a person would. That avoids the flood of false alarms from pixel-by-pixel comparison, where tiny rendering differences trip every check.

item.title: Aurora Solar
item.description:
Aurora Solar is used by solar installers, designers, and sales teams. A designer enters an address and the software builds a 3D model of the property from aerial imagery and lidar data, including trees and nearby buildings that cast shade. It then lays out panels, models how much electricity the system will produce across the year, and calculates savings and payback so a homeowner sees the economics.

Aurora automates much of the work that used to take hours. AI generates roof models and code-compliant panel layouts in minutes, handles stringing and fire pathways, and prepares permit-ready plan sets. Sales tools produce branded proposals and handle financing options and contracts, and drone mapping can capture detail for larger or more complex sites. For commercial projects, the platform covers larger arrays and different incentives.

item.title: AWS Rekognition
item.description: Rekognition lets developers add image and video analysis to an application without training a model from scratch. You send an image or a video and get back detected objects and scenes, text found in the picture, faces with attributes such as glasses or smiling, and flags for unsafe or inappropriate content. It works on photos, stored video files, and live video streams, and it integrates with S3, Lambda, and other AWS services.

item.title: Azure Content Moderator
item.description:
Content Moderator was Microsoft’s tool for checking user-generated content. It scanned text for profanity and personal data, analyzed images for adult or racy content, and screened video, returning scores and flags that platforms could use to filter or send items for human review. Online communities, marketplaces, and apps with user uploads used it as an automated first line of defense.

Microsoft has deprecated the service and no longer allows new projects, directing customers to Azure AI Content Safety. The newer service uses more advanced models, handles multiple severity levels across categories such as hate, sexual content, violence, and self-harm, supports many more languages, and adds features aimed at generative AI, including prompt shields and groundedness detection. Existing Content Moderator projects continue to work until the retirement date.

item.title: Be My Eyes
item.description: Be My Eyes connects people who cannot see well with help. In the app, a blind or low-vision user can start a video call, and a sighted volunteer sees through the camera and helps with a task such as reading an expiry date, matching colors, finding a dropped item, or navigating an unfamiliar place. Millions of volunteers around the world have signed up, which means that help is usually available quickly, at any hour.

item.title: Clarifai
item.description: Clarifai started as an image recognition API and has grown into a broader AI platform. Teams use it to find and call models for vision, language, and audio tasks, to train their own models on labeled data, and to run them in production. It includes tools for organizing and labeling data, searching images and video, and building workflows that chain several models together. Industries such as retail, media, and public sector have used it to classify content and find objects in large collections.

item.title: Coggle
item.description:
Coggle keeps mind mapping simple. In the browser, you start with a central idea and add branches by clicking, using colors, images, and text, and the diagram grows into a tidy tree. It can also draw flowcharts, with free-form connections between nodes, so the same tool covers brainstorming, note taking, planning, and basic process diagrams. The look is clean, with auto-arranged branches that make diagrams easy to read.

Collaboration is a core feature. Several people can edit the same diagram at once and see each other’s changes, and a full history lets you review and restore earlier versions. Diagrams can include notes and images, be shared by link, and be exported as PDF, image, or text outlines. Students, teachers, and small teams use it for study notes, lesson plans, and project outlines.

item.title: Creately
item.description:
Creately combines diagramming and whiteboarding in one workspace. You can draw flowcharts, org charts, mind maps, UML diagrams, process maps, wireframes, and more using shape libraries and templates, then connect them with smart connectors that stay attached when you move things. An infinite canvas supports brainstorming and planning, and teams can edit together in real time with comments and cursors.

Some features go beyond plain drawing. Diagrams can be linked to data, so a shape can show information from a spreadsheet or tool, and cards and tables let you build lightweight planning boards. AI features generate a diagram from a text description, summarize or expand notes, and suggest ideas for brainstorming. Presentations and exports in common formats help you share work, and integrations connect with Slack, Confluence, Google Workspace, and Microsoft Teams.

item.title: CVAT
item.description: CVAT was created at Intel and released as open source, and is now maintained by a company called CVAT.ai along with a community. It is a web-based tool for labeling data for computer vision: drawing bounding boxes, polygons, polylines, points, and masks, and tagging images or video frames with classes. It handles tasks such as object detection, segmentation, tracking across video, and classification, and exports to common formats such as COCO, YOLO, and Pascal VOC.

item.title: Dune Analytics
item.description:
Dune made blockchain data accessible. Raw on-chain information is hard to work with, so Dune indexes data from many blockchains into databases that anyone can query with SQL. Users write queries to answer questions such as how many people used a decentralized exchange last week or how much value is locked in a protocol, and publish results as charts on dashboards that others can fork and extend.

The community aspect is a key feature. Analysts share dashboards openly, so you can find ready-made views of NFT markets, stablecoin flows, protocol metrics, and more, and learn from other people’s queries. Dune AI features help generate and explain SQL from natural language, and APIs allow developers to use query results in applications. Data teams use it for research and reporting.

item.title: Hive Moderation
item.description:
Hive offers content moderation as an API. A platform sends user uploads, such as photos, videos, livestreams, comments, or audio, and Hive returns classifications with confidence scores across categories like nudity, violence, hate symbols, drugs, and self-harm. Companies use these results to automatically remove content, send borderline cases to human reviewers, or restrict access, which would be impossible to do manually at scale.

The company’s models have broadened beyond traditional moderation. Hive offers AI-generated content detection to identify synthetic images, video, and audio, deepfake detection used by government and media customers, and tools for brand safety and contextual advertising. It trains on large human-labeled datasets, and customers can customize settings for their own policies.

item.title: Labelbox
item.description:
Labelbox helps AI teams turn raw data into labeled datasets. Its tools let annotators draw boxes and masks on images and video, tag text, transcribe audio, and rate model responses. Project management features assign work, review quality, and measure agreement between labelers, so teams can catch mistakes early. The platform supports both in-house labelers and external workforces.

The company has focused on generative AI. Tools support reinforcement learning from human feedback and model evaluation, where experts compare and rank responses, and a labeling service provides specialist annotators for domains such as coding, math, and medicine. Model-assisted labeling uses a model to pre-label data so humans only correct it, and data curation tools help find the most valuable examples. Integrations connect with cloud storage and ML pipelines.

item.title: Landing AI
item.description:
Landing AI is built around data-centric AI, the idea that improving the quality of training data often matters more than tweaking models. Its LandingLens platform lets manufacturing, agriculture, and healthcare teams train computer vision models for tasks like detecting defects, counting objects, and classifying images, with a no-code interface that emphasizes labeling quality and error analysis. Domain experts can build models without being machine learning engineers.

The company has expanded into document intelligence. Its agentic document extraction uses vision and language models to read complex documents such as financial statements, forms, and reports, and to turn them into structured data with visual grounding that shows where each value came from. Developers use APIs to add this to workflows.

item.title: Mapbox
item.description:
Mapbox is the mapping toolkit behind many apps. Developers use its SDKs to embed interactive maps in websites and in iOS and Android apps, with control over styles, layers, and data. Mapbox Studio lets designers customize map appearance, while vector tiles keep maps fast and sharp. Companies in logistics, travel, real estate, and mobility use it to show routes, locations, and live data.

The platform goes beyond display. APIs handle geocoding and search, turn-by-turn navigation, route optimization, isochrones that show how far you can get in a given time, and traffic-aware directions. A navigation SDK supports in-app guidance, and tools for working with large geospatial datasets allow analysis and visualization. Machine learning is used for features such as map matching and road data updates, and recent products add AI assistants for developers.

item.title: Maxar Technologies
item.description:
Maxar was best known for high-resolution satellite imagery. Its WorldView satellites photographed the Earth in great detail, and governments, news organizations, mapmakers, and businesses used the images for defense and intelligence, disaster response, agriculture, infrastructure monitoring, and navigation. Maxar’s imagery supported mapping products and was often seen in news coverage of conflicts and natural disasters.

Its other major business was space systems: building satellites and spacecraft components for communications, observation, and exploration. Machine learning was applied to extract features such as buildings, roads, and vehicles from imagery at scale, and to create 3D models of the Earth. The company was taken private by a private equity firm and later separated its two main businesses under new names.

item.title: MindMeister
item.description:
MindMeister helps you think in branches. You start with a central topic and add connected ideas around it, using keyboard shortcuts to build a map quickly. Maps can be formatted with colors, icons, images, links, and notes, rearranged freely, and turned into outlines. People use it for brainstorming, studying, project planning, meeting notes, and mapping out content such as articles or courses.

Collaboration is a core strength. Several people can edit a map at once, with comments and voting to gather input, and maps can be shared by link. A presentation mode turns a map into slides, and tasks can be assigned on map nodes and synced with the project tools in the same suite. Integrations connect with Google Workspace, Microsoft Teams, and other apps, and exports include PDF, image, and Word formats. AI features suggest ideas and generate map structures from a topic.

item.title: Nearmap
item.description:
Nearmap captures aerial photos from aircraft, covering large areas in populated regions, and refreshes them regularly. Users view and measure current imagery on a map, compare dates to see change over time, and download data for analysis.

AI turns pictures into data. Models detect features such as roof condition, solar panels, pools, vegetation, and building footprints, giving insurers, councils, and contractors information without visiting sites. The data is available through a web app, APIs, and integrations with GIS and other tools.

item.title: Niantic Lightship
item.description:
Lightship began as a set of tools for building location-based AR experiences. The ARDK SDK for Unity offered features such as depth sensing, occlusion, and meshing, and the Visual Positioning System let apps determine a device’s precise location and orientation by matching camera images to a map of the real world. The technology came from the infrastructure behind Pokémon GO and drew on scans collected from players.

Niantic’s geospatial work later moved into a separate company, Niantic Spatial, after the games business was sold. The developer platform was renamed the Niantic Spatial Platform, with an SDK for Unity, tools for scanning places through Scaniverse, and mapping services. The original Lightship website was shut down, and visitors are redirected, with guidance for migrating projects.

item.title: Perfect Corp
item.description:
Perfect Corp makes AI and augmented reality tools for beauty and fashion. Its skin analysis reads a selfie, scores concerns, and recommends products, while virtual try-on shows makeup, hair color, and accessories on the user’s face in real time.

Brands embed the technology in their websites, apps, and in-store screens to help shoppers choose and reduce returns. Clinics use simulations to show likely effects of treatments. The company also owns the YouCam consumer apps.

item.title: PromptHero
item.description:
PromptHero started as a search engine for AI image prompts. You can browse a huge gallery of generated images, each shown with the prompt and settings that created it, and search for styles or subjects. That makes it a learning tool: you can see how others phrase things to get a certain look, and adapt their prompts to your own ideas.

The site has added features around the community. Users upload their creations, follow artists, and join challenges, and a generator lets you create images directly on the site using several models. Courses and guides teach prompt writing and workflow tips for different tools, and a paid tier offers more generations and features.

item.title: Satellogic
item.description:
Satellogic builds and operates its own satellites with the goal of making high-resolution imagery affordable and frequent. Its NewSat satellites capture sharp images and multispectral and hyperspectral data, and the company has emphasized low production costs, which allows it to launch many satellites and offer tasking and archive imagery. Customers use the data for mapping, agriculture, infrastructure monitoring, defense, and environmental analysis.

The company layers analytics on top of imagery. Machine learning detects objects and changes, such as new construction or vehicle movement, and produces insights at scale, and cloud tools and APIs let customers search the archive and request new captures. It also provides satellites and data to government customers for sovereign needs.

item.title: Shorthand
item.description:
Shorthand makes it possible to create the kind of immersive web story that once required a design and development team. You assemble a story from sections with full-width images, video backgrounds, parallax effects, and text, and the platform handles responsive layout and animation. The finished piece is published as a webpage that scrolls like a magazine feature, and works on phones and desktops.

Newsrooms, universities, nonprofits, and corporate communications teams use it for long-form journalism, annual reports, campaign stories, and case studies. Collaboration features let writers and editors work together with review stages, brand themes keep designs consistent, and analytics show readership. Stories can be embedded in a site or hosted by Shorthand, and a CMS integration helps publishing.

item.title: Storybird
item.description:
Storybird approaches writing through pictures. Writers choose artwork from a library of illustrations and build a story around it, which lowers the barrier for young children who find a blank page daunting. The platform offers story types such as picture books, chapter books, and poetry, along with prompts and challenges to get ideas flowing, and finished stories can be published, shared, and read.

Education has been a major focus. Teachers use Storybird to run writing assignments, give feedback, and manage classes, with lessons, quizzes, and activities that support literacy skills. Students can write and publish in a safe, teacher-moderated environment. Newer features introduce AI assistance for prompts and feedback, with a focus on supporting rather than replacing the student’s writing.

item.title: XMind
item.description:
XMind is a long-standing mind mapping tool known for its range of layouts. Start with a central idea and branch outward, or switch to another structure such as a logic chart, fishbone diagram, matrix, tree chart, or timeline to fit the problem. It has a polished interface, attractive themes, and features such as markers, stickers, notes, and attachments, and it works offline.

Special modes help with presentation and organization. Brainstorming mode captures ideas quickly, outline view turns a map into a list, and Zen mode removes distractions. A presentation feature plays the map as a slideshow, and exports cover PDF, images, Word, and Markdown. AI features can generate a map from a topic, expand a branch with suggestions, and summarize content into a structure.

item.title: 10Web
item.description:
10Web combines site generation with hosting. You describe a business or enter the address of an existing website, and the AI builds a WordPress site with layout, text, and images, which you can then edit with a visual builder based on Elementor. The result is a standard WordPress site, so it can use the plugin and theme ecosystem and can be moved elsewhere.

Hosting and optimization are part of the package. Sites run on managed WordPress hosting with a focus on speed, including automatic optimization of images and code to improve page speed scores, and tools for backups and security. AI features generate copy, images, and SEO suggestions, and an assistant can edit pages based on instructions. Agencies can white-label the platform and manage client sites, and there is an API for builders who want to embed it.

item.title: Adalo
item.description:
Adalo lets people without programming skills build mobile apps. You design screens with a drag-and-drop editor, add components such as lists, forms, and buttons, set up a database for your data, and define what happens when users interact. It handles user accounts, payments, and push notifications, and produces apps that can be published to the Apple App Store and Google Play, as well as web apps.

AI features speed up the first draft: you can describe an app and have the builder generate screens and data structures, then refine them manually. A marketplace of components and integrations extends functionality, and connections to external databases and APIs allow more complex apps. Typical projects include community directories, booking apps, marketplaces, internal tools, and simple social apps.

item.title: AdCreative.ai
item.description:
AdCreative.ai is aimed at marketers who need many ad variations quickly. You enter your brand colors, logo, and product details, and it produces sets of banners and social ads in different sizes, along with headlines and body text. Instead of starting from a blank canvas, you choose from designs and tweak them. That volume is useful for testing, since ad performance often depends on trying many variations.

What sets it apart is scoring. A creative score estimates how well each design is likely to perform, based on models trained on ad performance data, and insights tools suggest what to change. If you connect your ad accounts, the system can learn which visuals and copy work for your audience, and competitor insights show what rivals are running. Newer features add product photoshoots and user-generated-style videos made by AI.

item.title: Adobe After Effects
item.description: After Effects works on a timeline of layers that you animate, composite, and apply effects to. It is used for broadcast graphics, title sequences, explainer videos, social animations, and visual effects shots. Keyframes, expressions, and a huge plugin ecosystem give it flexibility, and it connects closely with Premiere Pro, Photoshop, Illustrator, and Cinema 4D, so assets move between apps easily. Many motion designers spend most of their working day in it.

item.title: Adobe Firefly
item.description: Firefly is Adobe’s generative AI platform. The Firefly web app generates images from a text description, extends or edits existing ones, creates short video clips, and produces audio and vector artwork. Adobe trained its own models on licensed content such as Adobe Stock and public-domain material, and it markets them as safer for commercial use than models trained on scraped images. Outputs carry content credentials that note they were made with AI.

item.title: Adobe Lightroom AI
item.description:
Lightroom is built for photographers who handle many images. It organizes a library, lets you rate and filter, and edits photos non-destructively with sliders for exposure, color, tone, and detail. Edits can be copied across a whole shoot, which saves hours after a wedding or event. Lightroom syncs between desktop, phone, and the web, while Lightroom Classic is the desktop-only version with a more traditional file-based workflow.

AI has changed the way people edit in it. Masking tools select the subject, sky, background, or people with a click, so you can adjust one part of a photo without painting a selection. Denoise cleans up high-ISO images while preserving detail, Generative Remove deletes distractions, and Lens Blur adds realistic background blur. Adaptive presets adjust to the content of each photo, and auto-edit settings give a starting point.

item.title: AIVE
item.description:
AIVE was described as a video enhancement service that used deep-learning super-resolution to sharpen detail, reduce noise, and raise the resolution of existing footage. That kind of tool takes low-resolution or damaged video, such as old family tapes, archival film, or compressed web clips, and reconstructs a clearer version. The idea is sound, and a number of products do it well.

The domain listed for AIVE no longer hosts a video enhancement tool. It now shows an unrelated media site, and searches turn up no active product of this name with the features described. A separate company called Aive makes a platform for automating video post-production for brands, which is a different kind of product. Because the original service cannot be confirmed, this entry should not be used as a recommendation.

item.title: Artbreeder
item.description: Artbreeder began with an unusual idea: instead of typing a prompt, you start with existing images and breed them together, like mixing genes. Each image has sliders for traits, such as age, expression, or lighting for a portrait, so you can nudge it in a direction and save the results. Children of images can be crossed again, which lets a visual idea evolve step by step. The community shares images that others can remix.

item.title: Article Forge
item.description:
Article Forge is one of the older AI article generators. You enter a keyword and optionally subtopics, and it produces a long article with headings, sections, and optionally images and videos, in a few minutes. It was designed for people who publish a lot of content, such as affiliate sites, small business blogs, and agencies that manage many clients.

Further tools support publishing. A built-in scheduler can post articles to WordPress automatically, an uniqueness check helps avoid duplicate content, and options control article length, language, and tone. A rewriting function can adjust text, and API access lets developers integrate generation into other systems.

item.title: Beautiful.ai
item.description:
Beautiful.ai tackles a common complaint about PowerPoint: you spend more time fiddling with alignment than thinking about content. Its slides are built from smart templates that rearrange themselves when you add or remove text, images, or chart elements, so the design stays clean. Rules keep spacing, fonts, and colors consistent, and a library of layouts covers timelines, comparisons, charts, team slides, and more.

AI features help create the first draft. You can describe a presentation, or paste in notes, and it generates an outline and slides in the app’s format, which you then edit. Teams can store brand colors, fonts, and logos in a shared theme, share slide libraries, and collaborate on decks with comments. Presentations can be exported to PowerPoint or PDF, or shared by link with view analytics.

item.title: BeFunky
item.description:
BeFunky is a browser-based editor for people who want quick results without learning Photoshop. The photo editor has sliders for exposure and color, crop and resize tools, and a large set of filters and effects. A collage maker arranges photos into layouts, and the graphic designer tool offers templates for social media posts, flyers, and cards. Everything runs in a web page, with mobile access too.

AI tools handle common edits. An enhancer sharpens and improves photos, a background remover cuts out subjects, and retouching tools smooth skin and remove blemishes. Artistic effects turn photos into paintings or cartoons, and an upscaler increases resolution. Newer features add AI image generation and a way to remove objects. Many of these are one-click operations, which is the main appeal.

item.title: Blackbox AI
item.description: Blackbox AI was built for programmers. It offers code completion, a chat interface for coding questions, code search, and the ability to turn a screenshot or image into code. A VS Code extension and a web app made it easy to try, and the free tier helped it reach a large number of developers. Users ask it to explain unfamiliar code, convert code between languages, write functions, and fix errors.

item.title: Bubble
item.description:
Bubble lets people build real web apps without programming. The editor works by placing elements on a page, defining a database, and setting up workflows that say what happens when a user clicks or a condition occurs. Apps can include logins, payments, and integrations with other services.

It is used for marketplaces, internal tools, SaaS products, and prototypes, and some companies run substantial businesses on it. AI features can generate a starting app or page layout from a description, and plugins extend functionality. Bubble hosts the app, so there is no server to manage.

item.title: Bubble
item.description: Bubble lets people build real software without writing code. You design pages by dragging elements onto a canvas, define what happens when users click or submit with visual workflows, and store data in a built-in database. That is enough to build marketplaces, internal tools, customer portals, and SaaS products. Because the logic is visual but still detailed, Bubble apps can be quite complex, which is why it has been popular with founders who want to test an idea before hiring developers.

item.title: Canva
item.description: For infographics, Canva works as a template-first editor. You choose a layout for a process, timeline, comparison, statistic, or report, then replace the placeholder text and swap in your own colors and fonts. The element library supplies icons, illustrations, shapes, and photos, and chart tools let you paste or upload numbers to draw bar charts, pie charts, and other graphs that update when the data changes. Because it is a drag-and-drop tool, people without design training can produce something tidy in under an hour.

item.title: Canva
item.description: Canva is a design tool for people who are not designers.
